mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues rising from its near-zero baseline while TRANSIT stays elevated, weekday travel and incidental shopping trips should expand, pushing RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not become less negative by the end of four weeks while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both remain above their t-3w levels.

mechanism_narrative: A further increase in RESIDENTIAL time signals more at-home substitution, which suppresses discretionary shopping visits and keeps RETAIL_REC flat-to-lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 7 points and stays above its t-3w level
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite RESIDENTIAL remaining above 7 and not reverting toward baseline.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT crosses back above 8 percent from a lower level, access to commercial districts improves and RETAIL_REC should improve within one week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the week after TRANSIT first moves from below 8 to above 8.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GROCERY_PHARM together with rising PARKS indicates local-trip substitution and neighborhood errand intensity, which can spill over into nearby retail visits and lift RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains unchanged or declines over 28 days while both GROCERY_PHARM and PARKS stay above their t-3w values.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in PARKS relative to the prior three weeks implies less outdoor discretionary activity, and that slack should translate into weaker retail-and-recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -13 after having been above -12
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the following 14 days even though PARKS stays below -13.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise together for two consecutive weeks, commuting-linked retail errands should build gradually and make RETAIL_REC less negative over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve by week 4 after both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT post two straight weekly gains.

mechanism_narrative: During a tightening-restrictions regime, an elevated RESIDENTIAL share combined with weak WORKPLACES mobility indicates reduced out-of-home circulation, which should depress retail-and-recreation mobility over the next week.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week while RESIDENTIAL remains above 5 and WORKPLACES stays near or below 2.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in GROCERY_PHARM above 14 percent reflects stronger neighborhood trip frequency, and that repeated errand pattern should spill into retail visits, producing a modest four-week increase in RETAIL_REC.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 14 for 2 straight weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not higher after four weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining above 14 for at least two consecutive weeks.
